note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: By the sun and its brightness
phrases.text: God swears by the sun and by its brightness. The commentators differed: some said the brightness means the day, and some said it means the light of the sun. Tabari takes the day, since the light of the sun that we can see is the day.

phrases.translation: and the moon as it follows it
phrases.text: And by the moon when it follows the sun. Ibn Zayd says this is an oath, and that in the first half of the month the moon follows the sun, while in the second half it goes ahead and the sun follows it.

phrases.translation: and the day as it unveils it
phrases.text: And by the day when it reveals her, that is, when it lights her up. Some philologists read the words as the day when it reveals the darkness, and Tabari prefers the reading of those whose words he has transmitted.

phrases.translation: and the night as it conceals it
phrases.text: And by the night when it covers the sun, until it sets and the horizons grow dark.

phrases.translation: And by heaven and ˹the One˺ Who built it
phrases.text: By the heaven and He who built it, that is, who created it, and His building of it is that He made it a roof for the earth.

phrases.translation: and the earth and ˹the One˺ Who spread it
phrases.text: And by the earth and He who spread it out, stretching it to the right and the left and in every direction. Some said it means what He created in it, and some said He who divided it up.

phrases.translation: And by the soul and ˹the One˺ Who fashioned it
phrases.text: By the soul and He who fashioned it, for He is the one who created it and brought it into balance.

phrases.translation: then with ˹the knowledge of˺ right and wrong inspired it
phrases.text: He made clear to the soul what it ought to do and what to avoid, of good and evil and obedience and disobedience. Some said He placed that within it. And the Prophet said that whoever God created for one of two destinations He makes ready for it.

phrases.translation: Successful indeed is the one who purifies their soul
phrases.text: Indeed successful is the one whose soul God has purified, so that he multiplied its cleansing from unbelief and sins and improved it with good works. Qatada says that whoever does good has purified it by his obedience to God. This is where the oath comes to rest.

phrases.translation: and doomed is the one who corrupts it
phrases.text: Indeed disappointed is the one whose soul God concealed and made to wither, so that he went astray until he committed sins and abandoned obedience. Some said it means he seduced it to evil, and some that he burdened it with sin.

phrases.translation: Thamûd rejected ˹the truth˺ out of arrogance
phrases.text: Thamud denied because of its arrogance, that is, because of the punishment that Salih had promised them. Some said it means their disobedience, and some that it means their wrongdoing. Tabari notes that the two words were chosen to keep the endings of the verses in harmony.

phrases.translation: when the most wicked of them was roused ˹to kill the she-camel˺
phrases.text: When the most wicked of them rose up, and that is Qudar ibn Salif. The Prophet said of him that he was a mighty and wicked man, inviolable within his clan.

phrases.translation: But the messenger of Allah warned them, “˹Do not disturb˺ Allah’s camel and her ˹turn to˺ drink!”
phrases.text: Salih said to Thamud: beware of the camel of God and her turn to drink. He warned them only about the camel's turn to drink, because they had already been told that the camel had the right to drink one day and they another.
phrases.ar: فَقَالَ لَهُمۡ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقۡيَٰهَا

phrases.translation: Still they defied him and slaughtered her.
phrases.text: They denied Salih in what he told them, and then they slaughtered the camel. They had agreed together to keep her from drinking and were content with her being killed, and because all of them took part the denial and the killing are put down to all of them.

phrases.translation: So their Lord crushed them for their crime, levelling all to the ground
phrases.text: Their Lord annihilated them for that sin, their disbelief and their denial of His messenger and their killing of his camel, and He made the destruction fall on all of them alike, so that none escaped.

phrases.translation: He has no fear of consequences
phrases.text: God does not fear any retribution for what He did to them. Some said it means the man who hamstrung the camel did not fear the outcome of his deed. The reciters differ over the reading, and Tabari says both are well known and correct.
